summary: Deep, high-quality Postgres module: trust-auth detection, cleartext/md5/SCRAM-SHA-256 auth with weak-default sweep, loot (databases/roles/pg_shadow hashes/extensions/replication roles/foreign servers/security-definer/public schema), COPY-FROM-PROGRAM RCE (capability + opt-in benign prove), lo_import legacy file read, dblink/postgres_fdw pivot with foreign-server user-mapping cred extraction, sensitive-column datamine with connection-string harvest, and a small CVE map. Gaps cluster around the wire-encryption layer (SSLRequest/GSSENCRequest never sent), the replication startup pseudo-DB, live topology intel (pg_stat_activity / pg_stat_replication / pg_hba.conf), several classes of hash and DB fingerprinting a superuser can trivially read, missing modern CVEs (2024 batch, CREATEROLE self-grant CVE-2023-5869 in wrong bucket), and cross-service wire gaps for hostnames/hashes/known_users derived from what the loot already sees.

missing_capabilities.name: SSLRequest / TLS-mode enumeration
missing_capabilities.description: The module never sends SSLRequest (0x04D2162F preamble) before the v3 StartupMessage. That single-byte 'S'/'N' response reveals whether TLS is offered, and follow-up handshake reveals cert (issuer, CN, SAN, expiry, self-signed), negotiated TLS version and cipher — and whether the server permits an UNENCRYPTED startup after refusing SSL (ssl=off, hostssl absent) or accepts weak TLS1.0/1.1. Same for GSSENCRequest (0x04D21630) in §55.2.11. Without it the module can't flag 'Postgres reachable in cleartext' — the single most common wire finding on internal networks and the precondition for MITM/downgrade of the SCRAM handshake.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: PostgreSQL docs §55.2.10 SSL Session Encryption; §55.2.11 GSSAPI Session Encryption

missing_capabilities.name: pg_hba.conf / postgresql.conf sniff via pg_read_file()
missing_capabilities.description: A superuser (or member of pg_read_server_files) can `SELECT pg_read_file('pg_hba.conf')` and `SELECT pg_read_file(setting) FROM pg_settings WHERE name='hba_file'`. That yields the entire trust table — every CIDR/host+auth-method+db combo, including `trust` entries that only apply to specific dbs (which the current trust-probe would miss because it only tries dbname=postgres) and replication trust that permits pg_basebackup. Also `SHOW archive_command / restore_command / ssl_key_file / log_directory` leaks filesystem layout used for lo_export writes.

missing_capabilities.name: Replication startup (replication=true / pseudo-db) probe
missing_capabilities.description: Send startup with the parameter `replication=true` (or `replication=database`) — the server enters the replication sub-protocol. If auth passes, the connecting role can pg_basebackup the ENTIRE cluster (physical dump: every DB, every hash, every extension, WALs) without ever executing SQL. pg_hba typically has a SEPARATE `host replication all …` line that admins forget to lock down (default 'trust' from Debian packages). Module currently only tests SQL access, misses this whole trust surface.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: PostgreSQL docs §55.4 Streaming Replication Protocol; §22.2.5.7 replication startup parameter

missing_capabilities.name: pg_stat_activity / pg_stat_replication topology intel
missing_capabilities.description: `SELECT usename, client_addr, client_hostname, application_name, backend_type FROM pg_stat_activity` reveals every currently-connected user AND the internal IPs/hostnames that connect (app tier, ETL, ops workstations). `SELECT usename, client_addr, application_name FROM pg_stat_replication` reveals every WAL receiver — standby DB IPs to pivot to. These feed hostnames/known_users/relay_targets directly. Module never queries either.

missing_capabilities.name: Hash-format classification for pg_shadow output
missing_capabilities.description: `passwd` from pg_shadow comes in three formats: `md5<32hex>` (hashcat -m 11100 with salt=username), `SCRAM-SHA-256$<iter>:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>` (hashcat -m 28600), or literal cleartext on very old / custom setups. Current code emits every hash as `kind=hash` with no format tag or hashcat-mode hint, forcing downstream tools/testers to guess. Also: distinguishing SCRAM from md5 tells you whether a downgrade attack against pg_authentication_timeout is even possible.

missing_capabilities.name: SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS channel-binding negotiation
missing_capabilities.description: Server advertises both `SCRAM-SHA-256` and `SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS` in the mech list. If a client with a TLS session selects the non-PLUS mech, the SCRAM auth is not bound to the channel and a MITM at the TLS layer can steal creds. Module blindly picks SCRAM-SHA-256 and never records that PLUS was offered but downgraded — miss both a hardening finding and a MITM opportunity for testers who own the network path.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: RFC 5802 §6; RFC 7677; PostgreSQL docs §21.5 (SCRAM channel binding)

missing_capabilities.name: GSSAPI / Kerberos & SSPI auth detection (codes 7,8,9)
missing_capabilities.description: _do_auth returns False on AuthenticationGSS(7)/GSSContinue(8)/SSPI(9). It should at least emit a fingerprint finding: 'server requires GSSAPI/Kerberos' + include the SPN (postgres/hostname) as a Kerberoasting/AS-REP-roasting seed for the AD module. Also GSSENCRequest support probe (see TLS gap).

missing_capabilities.name: CancelRequest fingerprinting
missing_capabilities.description: The Postgres v3 protocol defines CancelRequest (message code 80877102) that requires the 32-bit backend PID + 32-bit secret key from a captured BackendKeyData. Not exploited today. Also serves as a stealthy 'is this really Postgres' fingerprint (server closes silently rather than replying) to distinguish real Postgres from pgbouncer/pgpool/honeypots.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: PostgreSQL docs §55.2.9 Canceling Requests in Progress

missing_capabilities.name: pgbouncer / pgpool / pgcat admin console detection
missing_capabilities.description: pgbouncer answers a Postgres-like handshake but on `dbname=pgbouncer` accepts SHOW STATS / SHOW POOLS / SHOW USERS from `stats_users`/`admin_users` — often left as `postgres` with an auth_file that leaks EVERY pool password in cleartext or md5. Common on 6432. Not detected. Same shape for pgpool (9999) and pgcat.

missing_capabilities.name: Broader trust-DB probe (template1 / replication / common app DBs)
missing_capabilities.description: probe() only tries `dbname=postgres`. pg_hba entries commonly key on database name (`local all all trust`, `host template1 postgres 10.0.0.0/8 trust`). A trust rule limited to template1/replication/an app db is missed. Should iterate a small list: postgres, template1, template0 (rejected), replication (see separate gap), and the harvested `databases` list from any accessible connection.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: PostgreSQL docs §21.1 The pg_hba.conf File — record types keyed on database

missing_capabilities.name: CREATEROLE self-elevation (CVE-2023-5869 / 2024 CREATEROLE hardening)
missing_capabilities.description: Pre-16.1 a role with CREATEROLE could grant itself membership in any role — including superuser-adjacent roles — by creating a role, granting itself membership, then WITH ADMIN OPTION. Module already reads pg_roles; add a check for `rolcreaterole=true AND NOT rolsuper` and flag as potential self-elevation. Current CVE map has `CVE-2023-5869` bucketed as an integer-overflow (wrong CVE mapping — the string is right but the description is CVE-2023-5868/5870 style — worth verifying).
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: postgresql.org release notes 16.1; CVE-2023-5869 mapping vs CVE-2024-10978 / CVE-2024-10979

missing_capabilities.name: Modern CVE additions (2024 batch)
missing_capabilities.description: CVE map is missing: CVE-2024-10979 (PL/Perl env var manipulation → RCE), CVE-2024-4317 (pg_stats_ext / pg_stats_ext_exprs exposed sample data to unauthorised users), CVE-2024-7348 (TOCTOU race in pg_dump → superuser RCE), CVE-2024-10976 (row security policy applied inconsistently across queries), CVE-2024-10977 (client cert error → MITM injection). Also missing older-but-common: CVE-2018-1058 (search_path trojan-object — module tangentially covers via public_can_create but doesn't tie to the CVE), CVE-2021-32027 (array subscript arbitrary R/W), CVE-2021-3393 (partitioned-table constraint bypass row leak).

missing_capabilities.name: pg_event_trigger / ON LOGIN backdoor enumeration
missing_capabilities.description: PG 17 added `ON LOGIN` event triggers. Prior versions have `ddl_command_start / sql_drop` event triggers. A malicious event trigger owned by a low-priv role but firing under the connecting user's context is a classic persistence primitive. `SELECT evtname, evtowner::regrole, evtevent, evtfoid::regproc FROM pg_event_trigger` is one query.

missing_capabilities.name: Role-grant map / writable-table enumeration for low-priv accounts
missing_capabilities.description: For a NON-superuser credentialed hit the module dumps pg_shadow-visible bits but never asks `SELECT grantee, table_schema, table_name, privilege_type FROM information_schema.role_table_grants WHERE grantee IN (current_user, 'PUBLIC') AND privilege_type IN ('INSERT','UPDATE','DELETE')` — which tables the compromised low-priv user can WRITE (data-integrity/staging-of-payload angle) or `SELECT` across other schemas. This is the primary pivot from a scoped app account.

missing_capabilities.name: COPY TO PROGRAM / lo_export write primitives (distinct from read)
missing_capabilities.description: `can_write_files` is captured but not exploited; there's no finding calling out that write allows dropping an authorized_keys into the postgres OS home, planting a udev/pgpass file, or overwriting archive_command scripts. `COPY (SELECT …) TO PROGRAM 'cmd'` is a separate RCE vector from FROM PROGRAM (asymmetric grants exist in the wild).

missing_capabilities.name: Row-Level Security policy enumeration (pg_policies)
missing_capabilities.description: `SELECT schemaname, tablename, policyname, roles, qual, with_check FROM pg_policies` reveals RLS policies, and combined with `SELECT relname FROM pg_class WHERE relrowsecurity AND NOT relforcerowsecurity` finds tables where the OWNER bypasses RLS — classic privesc/leak surface, and the target of CVE-2023-2454/2455.

missing_capabilities.name: Untrusted-language ownership + PL/Python/Perl body dump for backdoors
missing_capabilities.description: Extension list already flags plpythonu/plperlu presence, but never enumerates the ACTUAL functions written in those languages (`SELECT proname, pg_get_functiondef(oid) FROM pg_proc WHERE prolang IN (SELECT oid FROM pg_language WHERE lanname IN ('plpythonu','plperlu'))`). Function bodies commonly contain hardcoded creds, S3 keys, LDAP binds, or explicit shell-outs.

missing_capabilities.name: libpq startup-parameter injection / options=-c abuse
missing_capabilities.description: Startup message accepts `options=-c<setting>=<value>` for any GUC. That is the vector abused by CVE-2020-25694/25695 and by more recent (CVE-2024-4317-ish) info-leak vectors — options=`-c search_path=` or `-c work_mem=` on servers that log them exposes information. Also useful defensively: probing `options=-c log_statement=none` acceptance tells you the server allows client-side log-suppression (post-auth stealth).

cross_service_wire_gaps: pg_stat_activity.client_addr / client_hostname — internal IPs and hostnames of every current DB client — never emitted into hostnames or relay_targets
pg_stat_replication remote_addr — WAL-receiver IPs (standby DB peers) — never emitted anywhere; ideal pivot targets

foreign_servers[].host is captured for pivot findings but not registered as a hostname/relay_target for the next scan pass; only propagated as origin_ip on Credential when a user mapping happens to have creds
pg_shadow role names (out['roles']) are captured but NOT pushed into known_users — the spray set never learns every DB role name
pg_shadow hashes emit with kind='hash' but no hash_type ('md5' vs 'scram-sha-256') — downstream hashcat has to guess the -m mode

datamine 'harvested' connection strings are added as Credential but the parsed HOST portion is never emitted to hostnames/relay_targets (mongodb:// or postgres:// URIs contain fresh internal endpoints)
email-shaped values in datamine samples never contribute to domains
TLS certificate CN/SAN (once SSLRequest is implemented) would emit hostnames and — for wildcard/internal SANs — subdomain hints for the DNS/AD module
pg_hba.conf CIDR ranges (when pg_read_file works) reveal INTERNAL SUBNETS trusted to talk to Postgres — a first-class relay_targets seed and never harvested
GSSAPI/Kerberos SPN (postgres/host@REALM) from the mech list would feed AD kerberoasting queue
priority_gaps: SSLRequest / TLS-mode probe — cleartext-Postgres finding + prereq for SCRAM channel-binding downgrade detection; single biggest wire gap and 3-line addition to the startup handshake

Replication startup (`replication=true`) probe — completely separate pg_hba surface with pg_basebackup → whole-cluster dump; commonly left `trust` on Debian defaults and invisible to the current SQL-only probe

pg_stat_activity + pg_stat_replication topology extract + pg_hba.conf sniff (post-super) — feeds hostnames/known_users/relay_targets that no other module can produce, closes the cross-service wire gap the audit called out

Hash-type tagging for pg_shadow output + CREATEROLE self-elevation flag + 2024 CVE batch (10979 PL/Perl RCE, 7348 pg_dump race, 4317 pg_stats leak) — small changes, high downstream ROI for cracking + version-based findings
notes: Module quality is high — the trust/loot/pivot/datamine chain is thorough and the finding text is actionable. Priority-1 (TLS) is a one-preamble add before the current v3 startup. Priority-2 (replication startup) is a second `_startup()` variant taking a parameter dict. Priority-3 (topology + pg_hba) is three additional _simple_query calls inside loot() plus emitting Host/Credential-style records upstream. The current CVE map's `CVE-2023-5869` blurb ('integer overflow in array modification') matches CVE-2023-5869 but the CREATEROLE-self-elevation angle (CVE-2023-5869/5870 in the November 2023 batch) is separately worth its own detection path against pg_roles.rolcreaterole. Not implementing anything per instructions.
